name: Fetch and read
desc: An address fetched in the background and the answer tidied by a NuGet package -- and not one line of code in the whole program. The box is bound to a value, every button is a rule, the table is filled by the rules that fill lists, and what is on screen is worked out from the values rather than set by hand.
vars:
address = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/owhs/axahk/main/version.json"
body = ""
fetches = 0
howMany <- StrLen(body) " character" (StrLen(body) = 1 ? "" : "s")
hasBody <- (Trim(body) != "")
looksLikeJson <- (SubStr(Trim(body), 1, 1) = "{" || SubStr(Trim(body), 1, 1) = "[")
said <- fetches ? fetches " fetched" : "Nothing fetched yet"

windows.name: Main
windows.title: Fetch and read
windows.status:
msg | Type an address and fetch it | grow icon=E896
said |  | right dim
windows.flows:
goBtn Click -> status msg Fetching...
goBtn Click -> assign body Fetch address
goBtn Click -> add fetches
goBtn Click -> addrow fetched {urlBox}|Fetched|{countLabel}
goBtn Click -> status msg Fetched. The window never stopped answering.
tidyBtn Click -> assign body Pretty body
tidyBtn Click -> status msg Tidied by Newtonsoft.Json, fetched from nuget.org.
clearBtn Click -> assign body 
clearBtn Click -> clearlist fetched
clearBtn Click -> status msg Cleared.
saveBtn Click -> saverows fetched fetches.tsv
saveBtn Click -> toast Saved beside the program
openBtn Click -> loadrows fetched fetches.tsv
windows.binds:
urlBox <-> address
bodyBox <- body
countLabel.Text <- howMany
tidyBtn.Enabled <- looksLikeJson
clearBtn.Enabled <- hasBody

kids.name: tip
kids.arg: Nothing in this program is written by hand. The address is bound to a value, every button is a rule on the Logic tab, and the two things it does are .NET methods made into your own functions on App > Libraries. Fetching runs in the background, so the window keeps answering while it does.

props.title: No code, and all of it is .NET.

kids.name: fetched
kids.arg:
{Columns: [{Key: "url", Title: "Address", Width: 460, Icon: true},
           {Key: "state", Title: "How it went", Width: 140},
           {Key: "chars", Title: "Size", Width: 140, Align: "right"}],
 Rows: [], Empty: "Nothing fetched yet. Press Fetch it."}

adaptors:
Fetch | new |  | System.Net.WebClient.DownloadString | address:string | string@async | Fetch a page or an API, in the background
Pretty | nuget | Newtonsoft.Json@13.0.3 | Newtonsoft.Json.Linq.JToken.Parse | json:string | text | Tidy JSON up, with Newtonsoft.Json fetched from nuget.org as the program runs
